newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London, Frankfurt stocks tumble; dollar down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London, Frankfurt stocks tumble; dollar down.

text.p: London and Frankfurt stocks tumbled by more than two percent on Friday as Wall Street opened with steep losses, applying a touch of the brakes to Europe's recent bull market.

In currencies, the dollar lost two pfennigs against the mark as traders were hit by worries about an increase in German interest rates. The U.S. currency also slipped against the yen despite concern that turmoil in Southeast Asian currencies would hurt the Japanese economy.

On a day when most European markets were closed because of the Assumption holiday, London, the continent's biggest bourse, fell by over 100 points to 4,881.0 and Frankfurt plunged over three percent on the computerised IBIS index.

Both markets chalked up losses in light morning trade, but took a bigger dive in the afternoon as New York opened with losses of 1.25 percent because of weakness in the bond market and earnings worries.
The change in sentiment contrasted sharply with the optimistic mood that has recently powered shares to record levels on both sides of the Atlantic.

London's decline was led by profit-taking in the banking and oil sectors. Banks, the engine behind much of the market's boom, sliced 40 points off the FTSE 100 index. Heavyweight HSBC Holdings was among the biggest losers, tumbling seven percent.
In contrast, the FTSE 250 index which incorporates mid-sized manufacturers and has recently underperformed blue chips, added 13.9 points to 4,703.8, a five-month high.
"People are looking to switch out of the main line and into the second line stocks," said Brian O'Donnell, sales trader at Schroders.
In Frankfurt, stocks took a bigger roasting as sliding futures, the weakening dollar and Wall Street's dramatic drop pushed the computerised IBIS index down by 127.89 points to 4067.64 at one point.
"A lot of people are running for cover out there at the moment. This is very quickly done -- it's a bit of a fast correction -- but just look at how the future has fallen," one Frankfurt trader said.
"Volumes are thin out there, but the momentum is strong," he added.
Currency markets also had a hectic day. The dollar fell to 1.8212 marks compared with Thursday's closing levels of 1.8417, squeezed by fears that the German central bank was prepared to raise rates.
Comments on Thursday from Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum were behind the latest bout of currency jitters.
Gaddum was quoted in a German newspaper as saying the Bundesbank was concerned about rising consumer inflation and would keep its options open regarding possible shifts to variable-rate repo tenders.
"The Gaddum comments seem to be giving a very strong hint that the Bundesbank is prepared to raise interest rates if they have to, and that's fuelling gains for the deutschemark," said Malpede.

The U.S. currency also weakened against the yen despite concerns a broad devaluation of Asian currencies could derail Japan's nascent economic recovery or force Japan to act to keep the yen weak, dealers said.
"Japan was having problems domestically, now they have problems in the region and that's more than enough to handle," said Jeffrey Yu, senior dealer at Sanwa Bank Ltd New York.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8212 marks and 117.25 yen, compared with 1.8417 and 117.85 in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 105.9 points at 4,885.4.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed down 78.57 points at 4,152.86. The computerised IBIS index was down 105.12 points at 4090.41.
PARIS - Closed.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $324.65 an ounce, compared to Thursday's close of $326.25. Silver was down six cents at $4.44.
